_readme: SHARED GOLDEN VECTORS FOR THE STREAK ENGINE. Consumed identically by
test/services/streak/streak_vectors_test.dart (Dart) and
functions/test/engine.test.js (Node). Only JSON-native types appear here:
instants are ISO-8601 UTC strings, canonical days are 'YYYY-MM-DD' keys, so
neither language needs a Firestore Timestamp to read the file.
THIS FILE IS THE SPECIFICATION. Regenerating it is the only sanctioned way to
change engine semantics. A change here MUST fail the JavaScript suite until
functions/streak/engine.js is ported to match, and MUST fail the Dart suite
until lib/services/streak/streak_engine.dart is ported to match. Never relax a
vector to make a suite green: either the port is wrong, or the semantics
changed on purpose and both engines plus this fixture move together.
Canonical zone: Asia/Kolkata, fixed UTC+05:30, so canonical day D begins at
18:30:00Z on the previous calendar date. Every instant below is a multiple of
that boundary plus a whole number of hours, so the arithmetic is checkable by
hand. All dates are in May 2024, a DST-free month in every zone CI might run
in.
'stored' is a schemaVersion-2 state document as the readers accept it.
'participants' is passed to evaluate() verbatim, NOT sorted or deduplicated,
so the step-1 refusals can be expressed. 'event' is null or {uid, instant}.
'expected.next' pins only the salient carried-forward fields; the rest of the
document is covered by the transition list and the per-language unit tests.
'restoreCostTiers' pins the tier table that GamificationService.getRestoreCost
and its JS mirror must both reproduce. The cost function does NOT live in the
engine; the table lives here so the two mirrors cannot drift apart either.

vectors.name: step1/self-chat is refused outright
vectors.notes: 1.9 / 2.9. participants collapses to one uid, so no mutual day is reachable. The document is returned untouched and changed is false, so no writer acts.

vectors.name: step1/a single-uid room is refused
vectors.notes: A degenerate participants list is refused rather than guessed at.

vectors.name: step1/a three-uid room is refused without destroying the document
vectors.notes: The reported count is 0 so nothing renders, but next is stored: count 5 and longestForRoom 5 survive.

vectors.name: step2/a one-sided first send records participation only
vectors.notes: 2.2. No anchor, no count, no deadline until the day is actually mutual.

vectors.name: step5/the partner completing the day starts the streak at 1
vectors.notes: 3.3. deadlineAt is dayStartUtc(mutualDay + 2): the mutual day itself plus one whole grace day.

vectors.name: step6/extra traffic on a counted day moves neither anchor nor deadline
vectors.notes: THE 1.2 FIX. sameDay is reported for observability; changed is false so the writer skips the write entirely.

vectors.name: step7/read-side derivation of an untouched active bond is a noop
vectors.notes: 2.15. event == null is the display and sweeper call shape.

vectors.name: step5/the completing reply on the next day increments by exactly one
vectors.notes: 3.1. alice already sent on the grace day; bob's reply makes it mutual and the anchor advances one day.

vectors.name: step7/a one-sided send on the grace day keeps the deadline where it was
vectors.notes: Deadline/break-rule agreement: participation alone never refreshes the deadline, so the countdown keeps running and the level falls to atRisk with 12h left.

vectors.name: step5/a mutual day after a 2+ day gap stamps the break then restarts at 1
vectors.notes: 3.4 / 2.16. brokenAt is the deadline that was missed (dayStartUtc(horizon + 2)), never the instant the gap was noticed. The lapsed count stays restorable.

vectors.name: step5/the double-break guard leaves previousCount alone on a restart
vectors.notes: 3.4 / 2.16. A sweep already zeroed the count and stamped the break at 2024-05-06T18:30Z with previousCount 6. Restarting must NOT re-stamp: step 5's break branch only fires when count > 0, so the live restore offer of 6 is not silently withdrawn and replaced by 0. No 'broken' transition is emitted a second time.

vectors.name: step8/one millisecond before the deadline the bond is still alive
vectors.notes: Break rule boundary, live side. Nothing is written.

vectors.name: step8/at the deadline it breaks, with no writer and no event
vectors.notes: 2.15 / 2.16. The anchor and the send evidence survive; brokenAt is the deadline and the 24h restore window opens from there.

vectors.name: step8+9/five weeks stale breaks and closes the window in one pass
vectors.notes: 1.13 / 1.17. The 🔥 badge on a month-dead bond: count 0, nothing restorable, history intact.

vectors.name: step10/24h + 1ms remaining is normal
vectors.notes: More than 24h left is exactly 'still inside the mutual day'.

vectors.name: step10/exactly 24h remaining is atRisk
vectors.notes: The boundary is inclusive on the atRisk side: 24h left is the first instant of the grace day. changed is true because only the stamped riskLevel moved.

vectors.name: step10/6h + 1ms remaining is still atRisk
step10/exactly 6h remaining is critical
step10/one millisecond remaining is critical, not broken
step10/zero remaining is broken and the count is zero
vectors.notes: 2.17. riskLevel == broken iff serverNow >= deadlineAt: a live count and a passed deadline can never coexist.

vectors.name: step10/negative remaining is broken and the window is still open
vectors.notes: One hour past the deadline: broken, and restorable until deadline + 24h.

vectors.name: step10/a broken stamp with no deadline reads broken
vectors.notes: A legacy projection that never recorded a deadline: riskLevelFor falls back to the presence of the break stamp rather than reporting normal.

vectors.name: step10/a bond that never started has no deadline and no risk
vectors.notes: No badge, not a broken badge.

vectors.name: step9/the last instant of the restore window is still restorable
vectors.notes: Step 9 uses a strict comparison, so exactly brokenAt + 24h has not expired. This is the live side of that boundary.

vectors.name: step9/one millisecond past the restore window it expires
vectors.notes: The expired side of the same boundary. History is not rewritten: lastMutualDay and the send evidence stay.

vectors.name: step11/crossing 7 emits the milestone once and raises the record
vectors.notes: 2.23. The engine reports; the paying transaction records into milestonesAwarded.

vectors.name: step11/crossing 30 emits only 30
vectors.notes: milestonesCrossed can hold at most one threshold, because evaluate only ever moves the count by +1 or resets it. A jump (restore 5 → 12, or a repair) is awarded by the writer performing the jump, never by evaluate.

vectors.name: step11/crossing 100 emits only 100
step11/crossing 365 emits only 365
vectors.notes: The engine emits the crossing even though the award value for 365 is still an open product decision.

vectors.name: step11/an already-awarded threshold is never re-emitted
vectors.notes: 1.21 / 2.23. The re-climb after a break must not pay twice.

vectors.name: bridge/a mutual day on the bridge day increments and clears the bridge
vectors.notes: 2.20. A restore wrote count 7, left lastMutualDay at 2024-05-05 (no mutual day is invented) and set bridgedThroughDay to 2024-05-09, from which the deadline is derived. The next real mutual day continues the chain rather than restarting it, and supersedes the bridge.

vectors.name: bridge/a restored bond still breaks when the bridged deadline is missed
vectors.notes: The bridge sets the deadline, so it also sets the break: brokenAt is dayStartUtc(bridge + 2), not dayStartUtc(lastMutualDay + 2).

vectors.name: step2/re-delivering the same event changes nothing
vectors.notes: 2.4 / 2.11. Structural idempotency: event.day <= sendDays[uid] is dropped, so no dedupe ledger is needed for the count.

vectors.name: step2/a late event for an earlier day is dropped, not double counted
vectors.notes: Out-of-order delivery. The event is dropped by step 2, so what is left is an ordinary already-counted day.

vectors.name: step2/an event from a uid outside the pair is ignored
vectors.notes: carol is not in the room, so nothing is recorded. The already-counted day is reported as sameDay and nothing moves.

vectors.name: repair/a negative stored count is treated as zero
vectors.notes: A corrupt document is repaired implicitly rather than propagated: count and longestForRoom clamp to 0 and no milestone is re-crossed on the way up.
